newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Jan-May oil deficit drops 1.46 percent.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Jan-May oil deficit drops 1.46 percent.

text.p: Peru posted an oil and derivatives trade deficit of $137 million in the first five months of 1997, down 1.46 percent from $139 million in the same 1996 period, the Central Bank said Friday.
The bank's weekly report also showed a $21 million deficit in May, compared with a $50 million deficit in the same month last year.
Peru imported oil and derivatives worth $301 million in the January-May period, a rise of 2.7 percent against $293 million in the same period last year.
Exports rose three percent to $164 million from $153 million in the same 1996 period.
In May of this year Peru imported oil and derivatives worth $43 million, a 51 percent rise from $22 million in the same month of 1996.
Also in May, Peru exported oil and derivatives worth $64 million, down 12 percent from the $72 million of May last year.
Peru reported an oil deficit of $347 million in 1996, up 10.5 percent from the previous year.
